title: Requiring Energy Infrastructure Providers to Obtain Rehabilitation Bonds Bill 2024
short_title: Requiring Energy Infrastructure Providers to Obtain Rehabilitation Bonds Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require corporations building large-scale wind or solar projects on private land to hold bonds covering the cost of rehabilitating the land or sea at the end of the project's life.

A proponent would submit a draft rehabilitation plan to the Minister 30 days before starting, then a liability assessment within 30 days of approval or any longer time the Minister prescribes, after which the Minister could direct it to enter a bond.

The bill would apply prospectively from 1 July 2025 to constitutional corporations and non-government land, excluding household and industrial roof-top solar, and would let states and territories impose similar obligations.
changes: The Minister would prescribe the format of rehabilitation plans and the consultation steps proponents must take with affected communities and landholders.
A provider could not pass rehabilitation costs on to landholders or lessees of the land under any circumstances.
Penalties would apply to providers that fail to enter into a required rehabilitation bond.
The bond would be discharged once an auditor's certificate satisfies the Minister that rehabilitation is complete, and the Minister could carry out the works where unsatisfied.
Ministerial decisions under the Act would be reviewable by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
summary.affected: Corporate proponents of large wind and solar projects, landholders and lessees hosting them, affected communities, and the responsible Minister are affected.
